children: Rocket Lab has been launching its small satellites for years, gradually emerging as a potential competitor to SpaceX. Now, Rocket Lab just scored its largest commercial launch contract in its history, signaling strong demand for small-satellite constellation deployments.
Rocket Lab secured a multi-year deal with Tokyo-based Synspective for 20 new Electron launches to deploy the company's radar satellites, the company announced Wednesday.

The agreement marks the largest commercial launch contract in Rocket Lab's history, as well as the most missions ordered by a single customer. Specific financial terms of the deal were undisclosed. The agreement brings Synspective's total contracted Electron launches to 47, the most of any Rocket Lab customer.
Shares of Rocket Lab rose 2.7% to $71.53 Thursday. Shares are up nearly 4% this year, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Rocket Lab will launch 20 radar satellites for Synspective to expand a satellite network designed to image any location on Earth within hours, day or night and in any weather. The missions are expected to take place over four years, with launches scheduled annually from 2028 to 2031.

Rocket Lab is a "core holding" for space bulls, Citi analyst John Godyn wrote in a note Thursday. He sees Rocket Lab as an industry leader, initiating coverage of the stock with a Buy rating and $105 price target.
Others on Wall Street seem to agree. Nearly 70% of the 23 analysts polled by FactSet rate Rocket Lab stock a Buy.
Rocket Lab said the agreement pushes its total launch backlog past 100 missions. It comes at a time when the space sector has faced a global rocket shortage and growing launch delays.
Rocket Lab's new contract builds on its long-standing partnership with Synspective. The relationship began in 2020.
